newsitem.title: DUBAI: Mideast Gulf Oil Outlook - Stuck at year lows.
newsitem.headline: Mideast Gulf Oil Outlook - Stuck at year lows.

text.p: Middle distillate prices in the Mideast Gulf are expected to flounder at year-lows next week as European suppliers snatch the lion's share of vital Asian import markets, Gulf traders said on Thursday.

Gas oil (diesel) prices have sunk to their lowest level this year at $23.10 a barrel fob Gulf, pushed down by weakness in the key Singapore market, now drenched by high stocks and unsold cargoes from the Mediterranean.
Gas oil's premium to independent Gulf price quotes was talked at 10-20 cents though Saudi Aramco was said to offered at 30 cents and Kuwait Petroleum Corp (KPC) at 35 cents.
One percent sulphur premium was at 90-$1.00 in June 1996.
"Aramco and KPC are trying to push the market higher, saying that for late July delivery recent premiums have been just too low," said one Gulf-based trader.

Though India's purchase late last month of 855,000 tonnes of diesel was to be mainly sourced from the Mediterranean, some traders saw a potential floor for gas oil premiums based on tendering by Sri Lanka and term requirements from Bangladesh.
Bangladesh Petroleum Corp's award of its tender for middle distillate and light ends supplies was also awaited as a potential source of support for the market.
"If KPC gets the gas oil it should improve the (spot) market for the next two months," said one trader.
Gas oil supplies from Bahrain were also said to be balanced, with supplies being sold into east Africa.

Kerosene, in contrast, had little scope for improvement and was expected to languish in a spring and summer demand lull because of the open arbitrage from the Mediterannean, scant Singapore buying and limited stockbuilding.
Kerosene, priced at $22.40 a barrel fob Gulf on Thursday, was talked at parity to a just a few cents premium to the quote, traders said.
Light ends fared better with naphtha steady at $188 a tonne fob Gulf as Abu Dhabi National Oil Company (ADNOC) and KPC looked ahead to finalising term supplies with buyers.
Naphtha prices had encouraged Aramco to offer spot cargoes of naphtha in Asia markets while bidding for gasoline to be delivered to the Saudi Gulf port of Ras Tanura, traders said.
